title: Source-first 14 m mechanical ornithopter interpretation

aspect_ratio.reading: The rounded 7.4 ft full span and original area paragraph's 6.61 ft² give b²/S about 8.29.
aspect_ratio.excluded: The inconsistent 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is not used.

wrist_span_fraction.reading: Rounded wrist-to-wrist span 3.7 ft divided by rounded full span 7.4 ft.

area_m2.derivation: The supplied 14 m engineering span squared divided by the source-derived aspect ratio.

photographs.principle: Broad constant-chord arm wing, rounded tapered hand wing, and the span/area and wrist proportions.
photographs.uncertainty: The printed conversion of wing length conflicts with the other rounded dimensions.
photographs.completion: The supplied helper's four-segment ellipse, taper 0.35 and 14 m span turn the proportion into production geometry.

photographs.principle: Curved-plate section data are contextual evidence that section force varies with incidence.
photographs.uncertainty: The photographed multi-axis low-Re chart cannot support reliable full-scale digitisation.
photographs.completion: engineering.json inner and outer coefficient tables are used verbatim and are labelled illustrative, not Stanley data.

photographs.principle: Compare candidate wing action against the force required by a target cyclic trajectory; retain the human-carrying purpose.
photographs.uncertainty: No complete design algorithm or validated coefficient set is present.
photographs.completion: Distributed strip forces and a 55 kg visible seated pilot implement the comparison without prescribing the trajectory.

photographs.principle: Powered straight flight has cyclic lift/thrust and therefore small speed and trajectory undulation.
photographs.uncertainty: Marginal handwriting is not treated as a quantitative specification.
photographs.completion: A finite 16 kW shaft model drives coupled wing coordinates; no direct thrust or altitude hold is added.

photographs.principle: Longer low-speed working stroke, equal cruise timing, force matching, and resonant wing/wishbone/body dynamics.
photographs.uncertainty: Several handwritten revisions and the continuation at the bottom are only partly readable.
photographs.completion: The supplied timing bias 0.3/0 and mass, spring and inertia values complete a fixed mechanical linkage setting.

photographs.principle: Resolve force from actual hand-wing motion; sweep fore/aft, close on recovery, exchange elastic/inertial energy, and allow body pitch reaction.
photographs.uncertainty: The text gives qualitative action rather than phase samples or dimensions.
photographs.completion: Explicit sinusoidal twist/sweep/stroke curves, overlapping rigid leaves and helper-derived Jacobians provide the missing phase law.

photographs.principle: Local incidence is adjusted through the cycle; incidence, section camber and thickness remain distinct.
photographs.uncertainty: The goshawk figure and its 13/10/9/6 percent values are an example, not swan dimensions.
photographs.completion: Independent supplied twist, camber and thickness metadata are used; goshawk percentages are not copied.

photographs.principle: A 5–6% arm section, thin slotted curved hand section, closing recovery, and conventional tail/rudder controls.
photographs.uncertainty: Takeoff angles and biological observations do not define a buildable full-scale mechanism.
photographs.completion: 5.5% inner and 0.8% outer metadata, two sliding leaves, three-wheel gear, horizontal tail, fin, rudder and pilot controls are engineering completions.

photographs.principle: Glide work is D times V and powered work additionally covers aerodynamic, trajectory and wing-inertia terms; a spring only transfers energy.
photographs.uncertainty: Missing appendices and rough efficiency notes prevent recovery of a complete power budget.
photographs.completion: Actual shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, transmission/damping heat and control work are integrated separately; the spring supplies no net energy.

engineering_assumptions.mass: 55 kg seated adult, 173.9 kg dry including pilot, 3.6 kg initial fuel and 177.5 kg initially wet are supplied assumptions.
engineering_assumptions.propulsion: The named engine, 16 kW continuous cap, transmission, governor, fuel model and all coefficients come from engineering.json, not Stanley.
engineering_assumptions.mechanism: The two half-length rigid sliding leaves, numerical phase curves, spring, mass points and finite-difference derivatives are explicit mechanical completions.
engineering_assumptions.visual: A triangulated steel/wood frame, exposed motor and reduction crank, cable king-posts, coherent gear, fabric wings and a recognisable seated pilot make the load path readable.

limitations: This is a favourable educational reduction, not a recovered historical design, structural substantiation or human-flight validation.
Steady strip tables omit unsteady wake, overlap flow, stall hysteresis, section pitching moment and flexible structure.
Roll/yaw inertia coupling and suspension are omitted; runway contact is a reduced three-wheel constraint.
Missing appendices, revised equations and experimentally validated full-scale section data remain missing.
